source.title: More Data Cannot Break a Symmetry: Identifiability by Design

record.tranche_reason: The study tests how stimulus choice affects measured similarity between model representations and refines interpretation of alignment results. It does not test convergence with model scale or capability.
record.gate_note: Directly relevant result: median distance between model representations changes with the stimulus set. The paper also reports split-half alignment outcomes, but those compare halves of the same representation, not independently trained models; those rows are marked none. No results test model scaling, cross-modal convergence, seeds, or recurring features.
record.test_reason: In one appendix result (Appendix B), the study compares 93 representations from 12 vision models and shows that their measured between-representation agreement changes sharply with which nine colours are used as inputs. That bears on V6, dependence of measured convergence on the input set. The paper's main subject is identifiability of unsupervised Gromov–Wasserstein correspondence, tested on split halves of single representations. That is not convergence between independently trained models. The authors state that the cross-model extension is untested (Appendix F).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors also stress three points. The demonstration covers colour and orientation, where the geometry is known. They make no claim that representational alignment is at risk in general. Extending the result to cross-model feature matching with natural-image or language probes is explicitly untested.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a design-time catastrophic-relabelling diagnostic and stimulus-set interventions, rather than testing convergence with scale or the original claim's cross-model or cross-modal comparisons.
record.method_sensitivity: The stimulus set changes both measured between-representation distance and split-half alignment outcomes. The paper also reports that small jitter of evenly spaced orientations raises design-time cost without improving alignment.

fits_no_version.finding: Unsupervised split-half correspondence recovery within a single representation depends on stimulus design. Catastrophic failures are 75.3% on the ring, 15.1% on a random draw, 21.5% on the geometry-discrimination set and 2.2% on the correspondence-optimised set. In orientation, they are 51.6% on regular vs 19.4% on uneven spacing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Symmetric stimulus designs make geometry-only alignment unidentifiable regardless of N or optimiser effort; breaking the symmetry restores recovery.

record.problems: The between-representation similarity comparison is reported as aggregate medians without uncertainty estimates. The split-half alignment experiments do not establish convergence between independently trained models. The authors note that a nonzero catastrophic-cost search result does not prove that no degeneracy exists.
record.rows_left_out: Other split-half outcomes, including exact recovery and mean displacement, are not recorded because they concern within-representation correspondence recovery rather than a named convergence version.

untested.parts: No sweep over model scale or capability.
No mapping between different models; alignment is only between split halves of one representation.
No feature, neuron or circuit matching across models.
Alternative similarity measures, neighbourhood settings, and out-of-distribution inputs; only stimulus-set dependence of rank-correlation RSA distance is tested.
No test of plateau, or of shared data or objectives as the cause.

missing.what: The authors interpret the ring's larger between-model distance as mostly within-representation instability (split halves fail three times in four), not stable between-model structure. This is relevant context for reading the V6 result.

record.verdict_notes: The V6 evidence is a side result. The direction is that the better-designed set raises measured agreement, rather than convergence vanishing, but it still shows dependence on inputs. The 93 representations are multiple layers per model, so 'between-representation' does not equal 'between independently trained models'. The orientation appendix reports only split-half and design-cost results, with no between-model distance.

versions.untested_parts: No sweep over model size or capability and no test of convergence across independently trained models as scale increases.
No paired image-caption vision-language comparison or scaling of both modalities.
No comparison of independently initialized training seeds.
The reported alignment uses split halves of a single representation, not mappings between different models or representations.
No comparison of recurring interpretable features, neurons, or circuits.
Tests dependence on the selected stimulus set, but not alternative similarity measures, neighbourhood settings, or out-of-distribution inputs.
Does not test whether shared training data or objectives explain convergence, or whether cross-model alignment plateaus.

It is not purely a comparison of independently trained models.
